name: Niros
why_it_matters: Set up by Ved Pardal on 1 August 1949 with ₹18,000 raised partly from his wife Mohini's jewellery — Jaipur's first multi-cuisine restaurant and the place credited with introducing Chinese food to the city in the 1960s. Still run by Pardal's sons.
insider_tip: Ask for the 1949 menu reprint — the kitchen still serves several dishes from the original card. Lunch is quieter than dinner; weekend dinners book out.
signature_address: MI Road, near Panch Batti, Jaipur 302001

name: Spice Court
why_it_matters: Family-run for 20+ years inside Achrol House on Jacob Road — the standalone restaurant most cited by Jaipur travel writers as the city's reference point for laal maas (Mathania-chilli mutton curry). Live folk performances most evenings.
insider_tip: Order laal maas with bajra roti, not naan — the millet bread is what locals pair the gravy with. The non-veg shorba comes with extra ghee on request.
signature_address: Achrol House, Hari Bhawan, Jacob Road, Civil Lines, Jaipur 302006

name: 1135 AD
why_it_matters: Inside Amber (Amer) Fort itself — named after 1135 AD, when the Kachhwaha clan founded the dynasty. Four sections: Shahi Aangan (sky-open courtyard), Swarna Mahal, Diwan-e-Khas, and the silver-and-gold Sheesh Mahal. The royal-recipe menu is researched from the kitchens of the Kachhwaha princes.
insider_tip: Sheesh Mahal private dining runs ~₹15,000pp; the main Swarna Mahal floor is ₹3,500-5,000pp and the same kitchen. Book a Friday/Saturday slot if you want to dine while the fort is still light.

name: Tapri Central
why_it_matters: Rooftop tapri-style cafe opened 2010 opposite Central Park gate 4 — hay-and-wood furniture, traditional thadi tea-glasses for cutting chai, copperware for water. The benchmark Jaipur cafe for sunset chai with Central Park as the view.
insider_tip: Sunset is when the rooftop is most photographed and most crowded — go on a weekday morning if you actually want to read, or aim for 4pm when the afternoon batch of vada pavs is fresh.
signature_address: Rooftop B4-E, Prithviraj Road, opposite Surana Jewellers, opposite Central Park Gate 4, C-Scheme, Jaipur 302001

name: Pandit Pav Bhaji
why_it_matters: Pandit Hari Narayan Sharma's stall opened 1983 outside Raj Mandir Cinema — the post-cinema pav bhaji of an entire generation of Jaipur college students. Several copycats now operate nearby with similar names; the original sits behind the stall with a covered seating area.
insider_tip: It's diagonally opposite Birla Temple, not inside Raj Mandir — multiple stalls share the name, so look for the original board with the founder's name. Order extra butter on the bhaji.
signature_address: Near Raj Mandir Cinema, MI Road, Jaipur 302001

name: Surya Mahal Restaurant
why_it_matters: On Panch Batti circle for 40+ years — Jaipur's most-named pure-veg multi-cuisine 'family restaurant' before the malls came. Crisp dosa with three chutneys, sambar from a separate vat for the South vs North orders.
insider_tip: The Italian/Chinese sections of the menu were add-ons; stick to the South Indian counter, which is what the kitchen built its name on. Filter coffee comes in a steel davara tumbler.
